confirmed.violation: Rule 164.2.b defines a Basic Rune's recycle ability as "Recycle this: [Reaction] — Add [C]", where [C] is one Power of the rune's domain (164.2.b.1). No Energy is granted; Energy comes only from the separate exhaust ability (164.2.a). In the trace, every recycleRune action on a Basic Rune adds +1 Energy in addition to the +1 domain Power, systematically over-generating resources.

Rule 348.1 requires that when a Combat Showdown closes (all players pass Focus in sequence), play proceeds directly with the remaining steps of Combat. The engine instead pops the showdown, returns to a Neutral-Open-like state, and offers the turn player `resolveFullCombat` as an OPTIONAL move alongside `activateAbility` and `startShowdown`. The turn player may activate arbitrary abilities and re-open fresh Combat Showdowns at the same still-contested battlefield any number of times before electing to resolve combat.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/combat.ts:227-257 (resolveFullCombat is a player-elected move, not mandatory) and packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:833-876 (passShowdownFocus returns to neutral-open without forcing combat-step progression; no Outstanding-task gate on activateAbility at :476)
confirmed.notes:
Rule 348.1 verbatim: "If it is a Combat Showdown, proceed with the remaining steps of Combat to resolve the phase." Rule 465.1 makes those steps Outstanding tasks. The engine does not do this — passShowdownFocus (chain-moves.ts:833-876) sets bf.showdownComplete=true, pops the showdown, and returns to neutral-open. resolveFullCombat (combat.ts:227-257) is then offered as a *discretionary* move enumerated alongside activateAbility/recycleRune, with no mechanism forcing it to run before other actions. activateAbility (chain-moves.ts:476+) has no pending-combat guard.

Trace confirms concretely: game-r2-0.jsonl seq=171 both players passShowdownFocus → showdownStack=[]; seq=172 available=[concede, recycleRune, resolveFullCombat(player-2-bf-ogn-275-298), activateAbility×4, startShowdown(same bf)], chosen=activateAbility(ogn-017). P1 then re-opened combat showdowns at the same battlefield at seq=175/185/190; combat only resolved at seq=193.

Note on the startShowdown-reopen sub-claim: it was true at trace-generation time (file mtime Aug 4 00:12) and was partially patched today in commit 3a900e9b (Aug 4 22:02) which added `if (bf.showdownComplete) return false` to startShowdown's condition/enumerator (chain-moves.ts:910,930). That patch blocks re-opening the same showdown but does NOT fix the core 348.1 violation — activateAbility/recycleRune are still legal alternatives to resolveFullCombat at HEAD.

confirmed.violation: Rule 355.8 requires that valid choices be made for ALL targets in order to put a spell on the chain; 355.9.b requires the target meet all targeting restrictions. Thwonk! (sfd-040-221) reads "Stun an attacking unit" — a mandatory single target restricted to an attacking unit. At seq=102 the engine let player-1 play Thwonk! and finalized it on the chain even though there was no showdown, no combat, and zero attacking units on the board; the chain item stores an unresolved filter {type:unit, filter:{state:attacking}} instead of a chosen target id. Per 358.1/358.5 the legality check should have failed and the play been undone; instead success=true and 2 Energy was spent.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/target-resolver.ts:60 (resolveTarget ignores target.filter, so state:"attacking" restriction is never applied); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:684 (playSpell condition relies on that incomplete resolver and does not require a bound target id)
confirmed.notes: Rule text verified: 355.8 requires valid choices for all targets to put a spell on the chain; 355.9.b requires the target meet all restrictions; 358.1/358.5 require legality check → undo on failure. Trace game-r2-8.jsonl seq=101/102 verified: pre-state has chain=null, showdownStack=[], both battlefields contested:false with only player-1 units → zero attacking units. seq=102 available[] offers playSpell for player-1-main-30-sfd-040-221 with NO target param; chosen=playSpell, success=true; runePools.player-1.energy 2→0; chain item stores raw descriptor {type:stun, target:{type:unit, filter:{state:attacking}}} rather than a resolved id; seq=105 chain resolves to null with no effect. Engine root cause: playSpell.condition (cards.ts:684-713) gates on resolveTarget(...).length>0, but resolveTarget (target-resolver.ts:60-140) filters only by type/controller/location and NEVER applies target.filter (declared at line 32, never read) — so {state:"attacking"} is ignored and any board unit satisfies the gate. Additionally the enumerator/reducer never bind a concrete target id at play time (no targets param emitted), so the spell reaches the chain with an unresolved filter, directly contrary to 355.8. Net: engine both offers and accepts an unplayable spell and spends its cost.

confirmed.violation: Rule 448 grants players the Standard Move (defined at 144); 144.4.b permits 'Units may move from a Battlefield to their Base'. The engine never enumerates a Standard Move option for any unit currently on a battlefield — no base destination is ever offered, and no bf→bf (Ganking, 144.4.c.1) is ever offered. Units that reached a battlefield are permanently stranded there for Standard Move purposes.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/movement.ts:156-158 (condition rejects non-base units); :206-258 (enumerator only reads base zone, only emits battlefield destinations); :286 (reducer hardcodes battlefield- prefix)
confirmed.notes: Rule 144.4.b explicitly permits "Units may move from a Battlefield to their Base" via Standard Move. The engine's standardMove implementation cannot do this: (1) condition at movement.ts:156-158 hard-rejects any unit whose zone !== "base"; (2) enumerator at movement.ts:206-258 only iterates getCardsInZone("base", playerId) and only emits battlefield destinations — it never reads battlefield zones and never emits a base destination; (3) reducer at movement.ts:286 hardcodes targetZoneId = `battlefield-${destination}`, so even a forced base destination would be mangled. Trace seq 46 confirms: player-1-main-22-ogn-147-298 sits at player-2-bf-ogn-275-298 (per seq 45 state), turn 5 Awaken has readied it, yet the available list contains standardMove only for base unit player-1-main-3-unl-002-219 with two battlefield destinations and nothing for unit-22. Minor caveat: bf→bf Ganking (144.4.c.1) is implemented as a separate gankingMove enumerator rather than via standardMove, so Ganking units are not literally stranded — but the core bf→base gap (144.4.b) is a clear rules violation with no alternate path (recallUnit is correctly non-discretionary per rules 616-619).

confirmed.violation: Rule 344 states a Showdown *begins* (mandatory) when Control of a Battlefield is Contested during a Cleanup and the turn is in a Neutral Open State. The engine instead exposes `startShowdown` as an *optional* player move, letting the contesting player continue taking Neutral-Open actions before the Showdown opens.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/combat.ts:121-130 (contestBattlefield reducer sets contested but never opens the mandatory Showdown); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts:885-934 (startShowdown exposed as optional; other neutral-open enumerators don't guard on staged Showdown)
confirmed.notes:
Rule 344 (via 319.8 → 323.8 → 323.12/323.13) makes Showdown/Combat opening mandatory during the Cleanup that follows any Move which leaves a Battlefield Contested in a Neutral Open State — the Turn Player's only choice is *which* staged battlefield, not *whether* to open. The engine instead defines `startShowdown` (chain-moves.ts:885-934) as an ordinary optional move whose enumerator merely offers it alongside every other neutral-open action; none of `standardMove`/`playUnit`/`recycleRune`/`activateAbility` guard on a staged Showdown.

Trace evidence (do_not_commit/wf-traces/game-r2-3.jsonl) verified: seq 44 post-state bf `player-1-bf-ogn-275-298` = {controller:player-2, contested:true, 2 units}, interaction.showdownStack=[]; seq 45-49 offer recycleRune/playUnit/activateAbility alongside startShowdown and player-1 executes all of them before startShowdown at seq 52. Seq 163 `contestBattlefield` sets contested=true; seq 164 still offers `standardMove` alongside `startShowdown` and player-1 moves another unit in first.

Current-source status: the `standardMove` reducer was patched to inline-open the showdown (movement.ts:335-350, commit 03967704 @ 2026-08-04 01:01Z — the trace mtime 00:12Z predates it, so seq 44-52 is stale evidence). But the `contestBattlefield` reducer (combat.ts:121-130) still only sets `contested=true` without opening the showdown, so seq 163-164 remains a live rule-344 violation in HEAD: after contestBattlefield the game stays neutral-open and every discretionary-action enumerator still fires. Same architectural gap will bite any other path that sets `bf.contested` without calling `startShowdownState` (e.g. setBattlefieldContested op, state-based-checks.ts:333).

confirmed.violation: Rule 383.3 / 383.4.d: when a Hold trigger's Condition is met, it must be placed on the Chain. Altar to Unity (ogn-275-298, battlefield) reads "When you hold here, play a 1 [M] Recruit unit token." When player-1 holds the opponent-owned battlefield instance player-2-bf-ogn-275-298 (which player-1 controls), the battlefield's hold trigger is never placed on the chain, even though a co-located unit's hold trigger IS placed.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:154 (desc.controller==="friendly" compares to card.owner — deck owner — instead of current controller; battlefieldRow owner set at trigger-runner.ts:174)
confirmed.notes: Rule 383.4.d.2.b: a "When you hold here" ability goes on the chain when the player that CONTROLS the triggering source holds and gains 1 VP. Trace seq 189 confirms: player-1 controls player-2-bf-ogn-275-298, VP 5→6, but the chain has only unl-043's buff (chain-21) and no Altar item; seq 134 shows the same card firing on the player-1-owned instance, proving an owner/controller asymmetry. Root cause: altar-to-unity.ts declares trigger.on={controller:"friendly", location:"here"}; trigger-matcher.ts:153-156 (object-descriptor branch) resolves "friendly" as event.playerId === card.owner, and trigger-runner.ts:172-179 sets card.owner for battlefieldRow cards from getCardOwner (deck owner = player-2). So playerId "player-1" ≠ owner "player-2" → return false. The self-branch at :96-101 already handles the controller≠owner case (per its comment), but the object-descriptor branch does not — it should compare against the battlefield's current controller for battlefieldRow cards.

Factory Recall (sfd-135-221, "Return a gear to its owner's hand") was finalized on the chain with no target chosen by the player — the engine auto-selected one of several on-board gears at resolution time, bypassing step-2 choice.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/target-resolver.ts:139 (auto-pick via slice); root gap at packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:804-807 and :855-857 (playSpell never captures/stores step-2 target choice)

Trace game-r2-9.jsonl seq 130 confirms: available/chosen playSpell params = {cardId, playerId} only; chain-8 effect = {target:{type:'gear'}, type:'return-to-hand'}; pendingChoice=null seq 130-136; player-2 had ≥3 gears on board (ogn-098 Energy Conduit, ogn-099 Garbage Grabber, ogn-101 Mushroom Pouch — the latter two still activatable at seq 160/125, proving they were in play); seq 136 hand gained ogn-101-298, i.e. engine auto-selected Mushroom Pouch.

In the trace, after the Combat Showdown closes the engine returns the turn player to a choice point where `resolveFullCombat` is merely one option alongside `startShowdown` (re-open Step 1 at the same battlefield), `activateAbility`, and `recycleRune`. The turn player can loop Step 1 indefinitely and take out-of-combat actions before damage is ever dealt.

(a) startShowdown re-open loop: ALREADY FIXED on HEAD. Commit 3a900e9b (Aug 4 22:02, ~22h after trace generation) added the bf.showdownComplete guard to both the startShowdown condition (chain-moves.ts:910-912) and enumerator (:930). Commit message explicitly cites rule 465.2/348.1 and notes the observer workflow was "reading stale wf-traces/". The trace under review predates this fix.

confirmed.violation: Rule 343.1 says the turn is in a Showdown State whenever a Showdown *or Combat* is in progress; 343.1.a says cards of all Categories, by default, cannot be played during a Showdown State. Between successive Combat-Showdown priority windows at a still-contested battlefield (Combat in progress — `resolveFullCombat` is on the available list), the engine drops back to a state with showdownStack=[] and offers/accepts `playUnit` and `recycleRune` as though the turn were Neutral Open.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/chain/chain-state.ts:131-146 (getTurnState ignores Combat-in-progress); packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:360 (playUnit relies on it)
confirmed.notes: Rule text verified: 343.1 "The turn is said to be in a Showdown State if a Showdown or Combat is in progress"; 343.1.a "Cards of all Categories, by default, cannot be played during a Showdown State"; 343.2 confirms Neutral requires NO Combat in progress. Trace verified (game-r2-1.jsonl seq 108-110): `resolveFullCombat{battlefieldId:player-2-bf-ogn-275-298}` and `playUnit{cardId:player-2-main-26-unl-029-219,location:'base'}` are simultaneously in the available list at seq 109; resolveFullCombat's own condition (combat.ts:240) requires bf.contested===true, so Combat IS in progress → per 343.1 the turn is in a Showdown State → playUnit should be illegal. Source confirmed: getTurnState() (chain-state.ts:131-146) derives turn state solely from showdownStack + chain and never inspects any battlefield.contested flag, so once the combat-showdown pops (showdownStack=[]) it reports "neutral-open" even though Combat is still pending. playUnit.condition (cards.ts:359-362) gates the standard base-play path on getTurnState()!=="neutral-open" and therefore lets the Unit through mid-Combat. (recycleRune falls under 343.1.b, not 343.1.a — its "any time" comment at resources.ts:137 may be an intentional mana-ability carve-out, so that half of the claim is weaker; the playUnit half is the concrete 343.1.a violation.)

confirmed.violation: Rule 313.3: 'A player who passes Priority retains Focus.' During a Showdown-Closed state, passing chain Priority should not transfer Focus. After the chain empties inside a Showdown, Focus should return to the player who held it before the chain (the attacker had not yet passed Focus).
confirmed.engineHint: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/chain/chain-state.ts:325-342 — resolveTopItem() unconditionally rotates showdown focusPlayer on chain-empty; missing rule 346.1 guard (no Focus pass when chain was opened by a triggered/Add ability). ChainState (lines 51-69) lacks an openedBy/openedByTrigger field to support the check.
confirmed.notes:
The observed Focus transfer at seq=22 IS a rules violation, but the governing rule is 346.1, not 313.3.

Rule check: 313.3 ("A player who passes Priority retains Focus") is a general invariant, but rule 346 is an explicit exception: "When the last item on the chain resolves and the turn returns to an Open State during a Showdown, Focus passes, and the next Player gains both Focus and Priority." So the claim's general assertion that "passing chain Priority should not transfer Focus" is wrong — rule 346 says it should.

However, rule 346.1 carves back: "Focus will not pass in this way if the chain opened as a result of a triggered ability being added to the chain."

Trace (game-r2-10.jsonl, verified): seq=19 standardMove opens a non-combat showdown with focusPlayer=player-1 and a chain containing exactly one item with "triggered": true (an on-arrival triggered ability). seq=21 p1 passChainPriority → focusPlayer still player-1. seq=22 p2 passChainPriority → chain empties → post-state showdownStack[0].focusPlayer = "player-2". Since the chain was opened solely by a triggered ability, 346.1 forbids this Focus pass; player-1 should have retained Focus.

Engine source: resolveTopItem() in chain-state.ts unconditionally advances focusPlayer to the next relevant player whenever the chain empties inside a showdown (lines 325-342). There is no check for whether the chain was opened by a triggered/Add ability — the 346.1 exception is entirely unimplemented. ChainState has no field tracking how the chain opened, so this needs a schema addition plus a guard in resolveTopItem.

Net: the trace behavior is a genuine engine bug. The claim's 313.3 framing is imprecise (346 overrides 313.3 for discretionary chains), but for this triggered-ability chain 346.1 applies and the engine violates it.

confirmed.violation: Rule 355.2.a: for a Unit being played, valid Locations include the controller's Base *or a Battlefield the controller controls*. The engine's move enumeration only ever offers `location: "base"` for `playUnit`, even when the acting player controls one or more battlefields. This under-generates the choice space for step 2 (Make relevant choices — 355.2), so players can never legally play a unit directly to a controlled battlefield.

confirmed.violation: Rule 465.2.c requires that 'Starting with the Attacker, each player assigns an amount of damage equal to their summed Might among the other's Units', with 465.2.c.3/.4 governing lethal-first distribution choices. The engine collapses the entire Damage + Resolution steps into a single atomic `resolveFullCombat` move taken by the turn-player with only a battlefieldId param — no attacker-first assignment step, no defender assignment step, and no pendingChoice is emitted, so neither player is given the assignment agency the rule mandates when facing multiple opposing units.
confirmed.engineHint: packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/combat.ts:364 (resolveFullCombat calls resolveCombat with no assignment input); packages/riftbound-engine/src/combat/combat-resolver.ts:96-136 (distributeDamage uses fixed sort order, no player choice)
confirmed.notes:
Rule 465.2.c verified verbatim: "Starting with the Attacker, each player assigns an amount of damage equal to their summed Might among the other's Units" — this is explicit player agency, constrained by 465.2.c.3/.4 (lethal-first) but still a choice when multiple equal-priority targets exist.

At line 364 it calls resolveCombat(attackerUnits, defenderUnits), which calls distributeDamage() (combat-resolver.ts:96-136). distributeDamage sorts by Tank→normal→Backline then iterates in that fixed order with zero player input — the assigning player never chooses which same-priority unit takes lethal first. The assignDamage move (combat.ts:183) is a bare reducer with no condition/enumerator, so it is never surfaced. No pendingChoice is ever set on the draft.

confirmed.notes:
Rule 402.2 says targets and other required choices for a triggered ability are made at step 2 (finalization), before opponents get reaction priority (406.4) and before the 405.1 legality re-check. The engine does not do this.

Source: `fireTriggers()` (trigger-runner.ts:297-312) pushes each matched trigger onto the chain via `addToChain(..., { effect: match.ability.effect, ... })` — passing the raw parser-emitted effect object whose `target` field is still a filter descriptor (`{type:"unit", location:"battlefield", filter:{might:{lte:3}}, excludeSelf:true}`). No target-selection step is invoked and no `pendingChoice` is set. When the chain later resolves, `executeEffect` → `getTargetIds` (effect-executor.ts:111-120) → `resolveTarget` (target-resolver.ts:60-140) auto-computes candidates and returns `filtered.slice(0, count)` — the engine picks the first match in board-scan order, not the controller.

Trace game-r2-9.jsonl confirms: seq 106 chain item chain-5 carries `effect.target={excludeSelf:true,filter:{might:{lte:3}},location:"battlefield",type:"unit"}` (filter, not an id); seq 107 offers player-2 only passChainPriority/recycle/activate — no target-selection move; seq 108 offers player-1 only concede/passChainPriority, so the opponent passes without ever seeing a declared target; after both pass the chain resolves and player-2-main-27-ogn-100-298 is auto-bounced (visible in seq 109 hand). Three units matching the filter were on the board at seq 106, so this was a genuine multi-candidate choice the controller was denied. The seq 185 First Mate (ogn-132) `{type:ready,target:{type:unit}}` case follows the identical code path.

Net effect: targets are chosen by the engine at resolution time instead of by the controller at finalization, so opponents cannot react to a known target and 405.1 re-checking is inapplicable — a clear 402.2 violation.

(1) Rule mis-cited. 323.11.a reads: "If as a result of the removal of Contested status there are Units located at an uncontested Battlefield that their controller does not control, their controller applies Contested status to that Battlefield." Whether that death check should use effective Might is a separate rules question, not 807.2.

The claim's own low-confidence caveat is right: root cause is spell-target resolution (playSpell never binds a chosen target to the chain item), not the 807.2 stacking rule.
